0.1 This

FOREWORD

Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 30 June 1987, after the draft finalized by Building Construction Practices Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council.

0.2 Sloped roof coverings using plain and corrugated galvanized steel sheets are generally used for storage sheds, godowns and factory buildings besides their extensive use in remote areas. These are easy and quick to erect and are economical. This type of construction is also popular in hilly areas and for temporary construction. 0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Minimum 300 mm length of sheet should project beyond the edges of For alignment of sheets, one piece of timber batten shall the purlins. be fixed projecting up lo the depth of purlin, on the first and last structural member ( trus or rafter) and with both these batten pieces a thread shall be tied to check straightness, etc, and then the sheets First, bottom layer of sheets shall be laid temporarily shall be fixed. by means of 50 mm long nails. After laying all the sheets up to the ridge, permanent fixing shall be done by means of J or .L honk bolts (scle Fig. 1 and 2 ). 5.2.1 For fixing of sheets The sheets shall be placed fixed with the edges turning Ihe sheeting is fixed and the the edges turning in towards the cover shall be not less than 85 mm. `alternate', one sheet (the lower ) being away from the bearer or purlin to which cover sheet on each side being fixed with the bearer or purlin.

5.1 Laying - The sheets shall be laid on the purlins

5.3 Sheet shall be fixed to the purlins of other structural members with ,7 or L, M6 or MS hook bolts. The length of the hook bolt shall be varied to suit the particular requirements. The bolts shall he sufficiently long so that after fixing, it projects above the top of tlleir nuts not less than 12 mm. The grip of3 or L hook bolt on the There shall be a side of the purlin shall be not less than 25 mm. minimum of three hook bolts placed at the ridges of corrugations in each sheet on every purlin and their spacing shall not exceed 300 mm. 5.4 The spacing of these bolts shall not exceed 200 mm.

5.5 Sheeting on steel bearers, where indicated, shall be riveted together with 6 mm dia galvanized wrought iron rivets and galvanized plain round washers ( two to each rivet ), at intervals not exceeding 200 mm for the side lapse, and on every corrugation (staggered ) for the end The sheets may be riveted in sets of 9 to 12 on the ground and laps. then hoisted in position. Care shall be taken in riveting that the sheet is well supported underneath and no indentation is made on the upper surface. Rivets shall be tightened and drawn closely and the heads spread evenly and equally. 5

IS : 12093 - 1987 5.6 All holes for bolts, rivets, etc, shall be made in the crown of corrugations and shall be drilled ( and not punched ). The holes irl the washers shall be of the exact diameter of the hook bolt. The Shrcr~ nuts shall be ti_ghtcned from above to give a leak-proof roof. Thev shall be shall not generally be built into gables and parapets. bent up along the side edges close to the wall and the junction shall *be protected by the suitable flashing or bitrtmen mastic `gola'. 6. RIDGES

AND HIPS

6.1 Ridges

and hips shall be covered with ridge and hip sections with a minimum 150 mm 1~~11 on either side over the roofing sheets, and shall be properly bent to shape and fixed. The end lapse of the ridges and hips, and bet\veen ridges and hips shall also be not less than 150 mm.

6.2 Ridges anti 11ips shall be fixed to the roof members with J or I_, lcici or M8 hook bolts. At least one of the fixing bolts shall pass through the end laps of ridges and hips on either side. If thts is not possible, extra hook bolts shall be provided. The end laps of ridges and hips shall bc joined together by M6 hook bolts. There will be at least two such bolts in each end lap. Iaps shall be set in red lead. The edges of the ridges and hips shall be straight when fixed end to end and their surfaces should be plane and parallel to the general plane of the roof, `l'hc ridges arid hips skia fit in squarely on the sheets.

7. VALLEYS 7.1 Valleys

AND FLASHINGS
ant1 with The and

ant1 flashings of plain sheeting shall be of witlth thickness as specified and bent to shape and fixed. They shall lap the corrugated sheets not less than 150 mm width on either side. end laps of valleys and flashing shall also be not less than 150 mm painted with red lead.

7.2 Valley sheets shall be fixed to the roof members below with 3 or L, M8 hook bolts. At least one of the fixing bolts shall pass through the end laps of the valley pieces, on either side. If this is not possible, extra hook bolts shall be provided. The edges of valleys and flashing shall be straight from end to end. The surfaces shall be true and Flashing shall be well ancl properly without bulges and depressions. tucked into joints of brickwork or masonry, secured with hardwood wedges and the .jnints finished neatly to match the adjoining work.
